title: The Old Dark House
byline: Universal Pictures / James Whale, 1932 — copyright L 3321 not renewed; public domain since expiry of first 28-year term

evidence.note: Universal Pictures Corporation registered the film as 'The Old Dark House U.P. 9 Reels', registration L 3321, application received 1932-10-13, first published 1932-10-12. Establishes renewal window as calendar years 1959–1960.

evidence.note: The Old Dark House (1932) is a sound film. The synchronized music and dialogue track are incorporated within the original film registration L 3321 (Universal Pictures Corporation, 1932-10-13); no separate score registration was found. The recorded track shares the print's public domain status through non-renewal of L 3321, the same registration covering the entire photoplayed work.
evidence.source: U.S. Copyright Office Public Records System, registration L 3321

evidence.note: The film adapts J.B. Priestley's 1927 novel 'Benighted', published in the US in 1928 under the title 'The Old Dark House' (registration A 1018678, claimant John Boynton Priestley, publisher Harper & Brothers (New York), first published 1928-02-02; ad interim registration A int. 10487, dated 1927-12-23). Renewal of the 1928 US copyright would have been due in 1956. CCE Third Series, Part 1 (Books and Pamphlets), Vol. 10 Nos. 1 and 2 (Jan–Jun 1956 and Jul–Dec 1956; identifiers catalogofcopyrig3101lib and catalogofcopyrig3101libr) were searched but the OCR text returned was truncated before reaching the 'P' surname entries; a Priestley renewal could neither be confirmed nor ruled out. Status remains undetermined pending a targeted hand-check of the 1956 book renewal records.
evidence.source: U.S. Copyright Office Public Records System, novel registration A 1018678

evidence.note: An Internet Archive item ('the_old_dark_house', Community Video collection, uploaded August 2026) contains a 1080p BluRay H.264 file (399.6 MB) and a Matroska file (6.5 GB), format and size strongly indicating a commercial Blu-ray source. Under Bridgeman v. Corel and Feist, a faithful restoration scan adds no new US copyright in the underlying footage. However: (1) any new supplemental material included on a commercial disc (liner notes, commentary tracks, bonus features) carries its own copyright; (2) circumventing copy protection on a physical Blu-ray disc is independently prohibited under 17 U.S.C. § 1201 regardless of whether the underlying film is public domain. A free, explicitly public-domain copy (Archive.org item TheOldDarkHouse, marked CC Public Domain Mark 1.0, uploaded 2018) is available and avoids both concerns.
evidence.source: Internet Archive item the_old_dark_house, page fetched 2026-10-06

watch.label: The Old Dark House (1932) — Archive.org, Open Source Movies (Public Domain Mark 1.0, uploaded 2018)

editorial:
Universal Pictures released The Old Dark House in October 1932, produced under James Whale's direction with a cast that includes Boris Karloff as the mute, brutish manservant Morgan, Charles Laughton, Raymond Massey, Gloria Stuart, and Melvyn Douglas. The film's copyright (registration L 3321, claimant Universal Pictures Corporation, first published 1932-10-12) was never renewed when it fell due in 1959–1960. The working explanation is that Universal had lost the adaptation rights in 1957—the 1963 remake was directed by William Castle, co-produced by William Castle Productions and Hammer Film Productions, and distributed by Columbia Pictures—and in the process destroyed most of its domestic prints; the title was commercially dead and no one bothered to file the renewal. Curtis Harrington discovered a surviving print in Universal's vaults in 1968 and persuaded George Eastman House to finance restoration of the film. The full nine-reel sound print—dialogue, musical accompaniment, all original footage—is free to screen, broadcast, or redistribute from a public-domain source.

The rights trap to avoid is the Blu-ray restoration circuit. A 1080p Blu-ray–sourced file (6.5 GB Matroska) circulates on Archive.org as of 2026, indicating that a commercial restoration has been pressed to disc. A faithful scan of a public-domain film adds no new US copyright under Feist and Bridgeman v. Corel, but the physical disc is separately shielded by DMCA anti-circumvention (17 U.S.C. § 1201), and any bonus material on the disc carries its own copyright. Use the 2018 Archive.org copy (identifier TheOldDarkHouse, explicitly marked Public Domain Mark 1.0) rather than a disc rip. One further open question: the 1928 US copyright on Priestley's source novel (registration A 1018678) may or may not have been renewed in 1956; anyone planning a new adaptation that draws on the novel beyond the film should verify the 1956 CCE book renewal records before proceeding.
faq: Can I screen, stream, or redistribute this film?

Yes — the 1932 print is public domain in the US; Universal's copyright (registration L 3321) was not renewed during the 1959–1960 renewal window. Use a clean, open-source copy such as the Archive.org item at archive.org/details/TheOldDarkHouse, which is marked Public Domain Mark 1.0. Do not source a copy from a commercial Blu-ray rip: circumventing disc copy-protection is prohibited under 17 U.S.C. § 1201 even when the underlying film is public domain.
Can I write a new adaptation drawing on the Priestley source novel?

Story elements as captured in the public-domain film are free to use. If your adaptation draws on content from Priestley's novel 'Benighted' (US publication 1928, registration A 1018678) that goes beyond what appears in the film, you should first check whether the 1928 US copyright was renewed in 1956 — that renewal status could not be confirmed from available records during this research session.
